title: Quantum computers are starting to become useful as scientific tools | New Scientist
description: Three problems that are out of reach for conventional computers have been cracked by quantum computers and show how important the machines could become for scientific research
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

title: First-of-kind Guillain-Barré drug switches off part of immune system | New Scientist
description: A treatment that turns off the bit of the immune system that goes haywire in Guillain-Barré syndrome may be the first targeted therapy approved for the autoimmune condition
author: Alice Klein

title: Flat head syndrome discovered in Iron Age skeletons | New Scientist
description: Certain sleeping positions can lead to babies developing flattened heads, and an analysis of ancient skulls from Italy reveals that this condition affected people in the 9th century BC
author: Christa Lesté-Lasserre

title: Spectacular fossil preserves internal organs of ancient marine reptile | New Scientist
description: A stunningly intact marine reptile named Austronaga minuta that lived around 245 million years ago may have looked like a miniature version of more famous later ocean predators, like plesiosaurs
author: James Woodford

title: Worry about what your children eat, but don't forget your own diet | New Scientist
description: Measures like bans on advertising junk food to children are essential for instilling healthy eating at a young age, but we shouldn't let adults off the hook when it comes to improving our diets
author: New Scientist

title: Strange three-lobed asteroid seems to have its own tiny moon | New Scientist
description: The asteroid 44 Nysa was first spotted more than 150 years ago, but we are only now finally figuring out its weird shape and mysterious formation
author: Leah Crane
